findings.title: GPU lanes fail open: CUDA-availability assert dropped in CI refactor
findings.claim: The 'Assert CUDA available' preflight that #424's fix (commit 847b464e) added to make Triton/CUDA validation meaningful was deleted when commit 76e013d8 (#600) rewrote the reusable test workflow; the current python-tests.yml contains no CUDA availability check (grep 'is_available|Assert CUDA' over .github/ returns nothing), so all three CUDA lanes — the only place Triton kernels, patched-model parity, and CUDA DP paths are validated — pass green when the self-hosted runner's CUDA is broken.
findings.failure_scenario: GPU-runner-001 gets a driver/toolkit mismatch after a host update. conftest.py:38 auto-skips every cuda-marked test (torch.cuda.is_available() False), pytest exits 0, the CUDA (locked/minimum/latest) lanes report success, the required python-tests gate passes, and main publishes wheels with zero GPU-side validation — indefinitely, since nothing distinguishes 'all skipped' from 'all passed'.
evidence: 847b464e added: '- name: Assert CUDA available ... assert torch.cuda.is_available()' and removed continue-on-error (git show 847b464e)
06ede505 moved it into a reusable workflow behind an assert-cuda input; 76e013d8 deleted that workflow and its replacement (current .github/workflows/python-tests.yml:97-128) has no such step
conftest.py:38: 'if "cuda" in item.keywords and not torch.cuda.is_available(): <skip>' — skips exit 0
pr.yml:137-150 / ci.yml:100-138 CUDA lanes pass allow-empty-test-selection: true and rely solely on the marker
findings.fix_sketch: Re-add a runner-scoped preflight in python-tests.yml (e.g. when inputs.runner is the GPU label, run 'uv run python -c "import torch; assert torch.cuda.is_available()"' after uv sync), or have run_python_test_package.sh fail the cuda-marker lanes when 100% of selected tests skip.

findings.title: dp-sgd.md end-to-end loop still broken (OPQ-144 unfixed)
findings.claim: The DP-SGD guide's only complete training loop retains every defect OPQ-144 documented: 'for step, batch in enumerate(sampler)' iterates the PoissonSampler directly (it yields list[int] index lists, not data — no DataLoader/batch_sampler anywhere on the page), the sampler at :107 is built without n_steps so iteration never terminates, the loop never composes the accountant or reads epsilon (unlike the DP-FTRL twin), and torchopt.apply_updates is called without importing torchopt.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader treats the skeleton as fill-in-the-blanks and keeps the wrong iteration pattern: their model trains on integer index lists (crash) or, after 'fixing' it by indexing manually, runs an unbounded loop past the 1000 calibrated steps with no epsilon readout to notice.
evidence: docs/user-guide/dp-sgd.md:144 'for step, batch in enumerate(sampler):' with sampler = PoissonSampler(dataset, sample_rate=..., key=...) at :107-110 (no n_steps)
grep -n 'DataLoader|batch_sampler|import torchopt|n_steps' docs/user-guide/dp-sgd.md → zero hits
The loop body (:145-148) contains no accountant composition; dp-ftrl.md's equivalent shows acct |= step
Page edited 4x in the delta (499f2d7f, 6fe85832, 1d216fcd, 764620f5) without touching the loop
findings.fix_sketch: Wrap in DataLoader(dataset, batch_sampler=sampler), pass n_steps=1000 to match section 1's calibration, add 'accountant = accountant | step_proc' + epsilon_at readout, and import torchopt.

findings.title: precision.md binds optimizer.update result as (opt_state, params)
findings.claim: The fp16 loss-scaling recipe still contains OPQ-141's second half: 'opt_state, params = optimizer.update(noisy, opt_state, params=params)' — update returns (updates, new_state), so params becomes the optimizer state and the updates are treated as state; every other doc page uses the correct 'updates, opt_state = optimizer.update(...)' + torchopt.apply_updates (11 sites verified).
findings.failure_scenario: A user copies the fp16 recipe verbatim; on the next loop iteration model_fn receives the optimizer state as params — a confusing structure error at best, and if pytree shapes coincide (SGD-like states), silently corrupted training.
evidence: docs/user-guide/precision.md:97 (current tree)
grep 'optimizer.update' docs/ shows every other site as 'updates, opt_state = ...' (distributed.md:100, dp-ftrl.md:242, dp-sgd.md:147, noise.md:85/:339, optimizers.md x5)
The same file was edited by 18f67eac (#681) and 6fe85832 without fixing the binding (accountant.advance in the same block WAS fixed to 'accountant | step_process')
findings.fix_sketch: Replace with 'updates, opt_state = optimizer.update(noisy, opt_state, params=params)' followed by 'params = torchopt.apply_updates(params, updates)'.

pyproject.toml:298 per-file-ignores '"tests/**" = [...]' is unreachable dead config given the exclude
